title: Normalise a path
description: Simplify an absolute path, a text that starts with a slash and has directory names separated by slashes. Empty names (from doubled or trailing slashes) and the name "." are dropped; the name ".." removes the directory before it. A ".." with no directory left to remove is an error with the message "path escapes root"; scanning is from left to right and the first such ".." counts. The result starts with a slash and has the remaining names separated by single slashes, without a trailing slash; the path with no names left is "/". Names that merely contain dots, such as "..a" or "...", are ordinary names.
notes: Needs a stack discipline (the Zehn reference pops by rebuilding the list). Names like '..a' and '...' must not be mistaken for '..'. Paths always start with a slash.
